name: Huang Ziwei
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Uroica Precision Information Engineering Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 300099), Tai'an, Shandong
profile: Huang Ziwei (黄自伟) co-founded and runs Uroica, founded in 1998 in Tai'an and listed on ChiNext in 2010. It makes coal-mine roof and rock-burst safety monitoring systems, explosion-proof monorail mine transport and mining robots, plus defence products. Hurun (2021) listed his fortune jointly with Wang Jinghua.
interesting_fact: Uroica, formerly Uroica Mining Safety Engineering, renamed itself in 2017. It has moved from mine-pressure monitoring into intelligent mine transport (including new-energy monorail cranes and self-driving locomotive systems) and defence electronics.
deep_cut_fact: Before he became an entrepreneur he was an academic: he graduated from Tongji University in 1982 and then became a professor at Shandong University of Science & Technology. That is the mining-engineering background Uroica grew out of.

public_contacts.value: http://www.uroica.com.cn (has investor-relations and 联系我们 contact pages with an inquiry form)

notes: Older executive (mid/late 70s per data sites). He has no English media presence. The best route is a Chinese-language letter through the company board secretary (Du Houke) or the website inquiry form. Company IR phone is +86 538 892 6152 (published listing profile, stockanalysis.com).

name: Lu Hualiang
current_role: Director and Deputy General Manager, Hangzhou Onechance Tech Corp. (壹网壹创, SZSE: 300792), per insider-data listings (since Feb 2016)
profile: Lu Hualiang (卢华亮) is listed as a director and deputy GM of Hangzhou Onechance Tech Corp., a Hangzhou e-commerce services firm founded in 2012 and controlled by chairman Lin Zhenyu. Onechance runs Tmall and other online stores for consumer brands. It listed on ChiNext in 2019, and Hurun (2020) put his stake at about US$310m.
interesting_fact: Onechance is an outsourced 'TP' (Tmall partner) operator. It runs the whole online chain for brands such as P&G, Pechoin (百雀羚), Elizabeth Arden, Shiseido and Amorepacific, from store design and big-data marketing to customer service and warehousing.
notes: Identity is only partly confirmed: insider aggregators (MarketScreener) list 'Hua Liang Lu' as director and deputy GM of Onechance, and his current board status was not verified in recent filings. He has no public profile. Contact him through the board secretary (Gao Fan) at the company IR email.

name: Xu Zhonggui
current_role: Co-actual controller and major shareholder of Shenzhen SZZT Electronics Co., Ltd. (证通电子, SZSE: 002197); the chairman is her husband, Zeng Shengqiang
profile: Xu Zhonggui (许忠桂, b. 1963) and her husband Zeng Shengqiang control SZZT Electronics. Founded in Shenzhen in 1993, SZZT makes payment and financial self-service hardware (encrypted PIN pads, kiosks) and has expanded into IDC/cloud data-centre services. She has worked at the company since 1997, and it listed in Shenzhen in 2007.
interesting_fact: SZZT's ATM encrypted PIN pad was the first in Asia to win VISA certification. The company also helped write China's national technical specification for PIN-pad systems.
deep_cut_fact: Before she joined SZZT in 1997 she worked at the Ministry of Electronics Industry's Jiannan Machinery Factory (电子工业部建南机器厂), then at Shenzhen Kaifa Technology and Shenzhen Anke High-Tech.

public_contacts.value: ztbank@szzt.com.cn (company email in the 2007 IPO prospectus; may be outdated)

notes: Very private, with no media presence. Her husband Zeng Shengqiang is the public face, so approach through him or the board secretary. SZZT's IDC/data-centre business makes it relevant to the podcast. Her current shareholding was not re-verified.

name: Oleksiy Martynov
current_role: Co-owner of Privat Group (Ukraine) and private investor; no current executive title published
profile: Oleksiy Martynov (b. 1966, Liudinovo, Russia) is a Dnipro-based businessman and long-time partner of Ihor Kolomoisky and Hennadiy Bogolyubov in Privat Group. He co-founded PrivatBank in 1992 and sat on its supervisory board from 2000 until the bank was nationalised. He has also run Solm Ltd, the group's ferroalloy business. NV ranked him 12th-richest in Ukraine in 2019 (about US$602m).
interesting_fact: He was one of the four co-founders of PrivatBank (1992), which became Ukraine's largest bank, after first co-founding the trading firm Sentoza with Kolomoisky and Bogolyubov in 1991.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an electrical engineer in automatic control systems (Dnipropetrovsk University, 1989). His first business job was at the late-Soviet 'Fianit' cooperative, before Sentoza and PrivatBank.
notes: Extremely private, with no website, social accounts or press office. Privat Group/PrivatBank shareholders are under heavy legal and political scrutiny in Ukraine since the 2016 nationalisation, which makes him a sensitive and probably unreachable guest. Alive status is inferred (no death reported in the 2021+ sources).

name: William J Maris
current_role: Founder and Managing Partner, Section 32 (venture capital, San Diego/La Jolla); former 10%+ holder of Dave Inc. via Section 32 Fund 1
profile: Bill Maris (b. 1975) founded Google Ventures (GV) in 2008 and was its first CEO, backing Uber, Nest, Flatiron Health and Slack. He also conceived Alphabet's longevity company Calico. In 2017 he founded Section 32, a frontier-tech fund (about US$2bn AUM) whose portfolio includes Phaidra (AI for data-centre cooling), Neuralink, SandboxAQ and Infleqtion. His Dave Inc. stake came from an early Section 32 bet.
interesting_fact: While at GV he pitched Google's leadership on Calico, a company meant 'to treat aging as a disease, and cure it.' Google funded it, and it became one of Alphabet's best-known moonshots.
deep_cut_fact: Before Google, he founded Burlee.com in 1997, one of the first web-hosting companies. He built its original infrastructure after teaching himself to code from books bought at his local Barnes & Noble. Burlee was later acquired by Interland, which became Web.com.
notes: A strong podcast fit: he trained in neuroscience (Middlebury), backs energy/data-centre-relevant companies like Phaidra and Infleqtion, and has appeared on All-In. Section 32 publishes no press email, so the best route is a warm intro or an approach via Section 32's site. Avoid personal-life topics.

name: Lip Bu Tan
current_role: CEO and Director, Intel Corporation (since March 2025); Chairman of Walden International and founding managing partner of Walden Catalyst Ventures; also listed as a director of Credo Technology
profile: Malaysia-born, Singapore-educated Lip-Bu Tan founded Walden International in 1987, one of the first VC firms to back Asian semiconductor start-ups. He was CEO of Cadence Design Systems from 2008 to 2021, and Intel named him CEO in March 2025 to lead its turnaround. He won the SIA's 2022 Robert N. Noyce Award and was on TIME's 100 most influential list in 2026.
interesting_fact: He began as a would-be nuclear engineer. He was at MIT working toward a PhD in nuclear engineering in 1979 when the Three Mile Island accident struck. A careers adviser told him there was no future in the field, so he dropped out, joined a nuclear consultancy in San Francisco and later took an MBA.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2025 NTU alumni profile he is 'the curious kid who became Intel's CEO'. He took a physics degree at Nanyang University in Singapore before MIT, and NTU says he has kept close ties to his alma mater.

public_contacts.value: Intel Public Relations contact form (for journalists)

notes: Very high-profile and heavily gated. Go through Intel corporate PR (the form; pressroompublishing@intel.com is explicitly NOT for media). His nuclear-engineering start is a natural hook for an energy/data-centre podcast. Walden Catalyst is an alternative route.

name: Alan Wells
current_role: Founder (former owner) of Sauflon Pharmaceuticals; private investor since its 2014 sale. No current title found.
profile: Alan Wells, an optician in south-west London, founded contact-lens maker Sauflon Pharmaceuticals in 1985. The company grew factories in London, Kent, Southampton and Hungary and sold in 50+ countries, and in 2014 the family (with Bradley and David Wells) sold it to CooperVision for about £700m. The Sunday Times Rich List has since tracked the Wells family fortune.
interesting_fact: Sauflon's Southampton plant produced more than 100 million contact lenses a year. It was one of only four companies worldwide making both lenses and aftercare solutions, and it supplied chains such as Specsavers.
deep_cut_fact: Sauflon started from scratch in Twickenham selling only contact-lens aftercare solution. Wells moved into making lenses as they took off, and after silicone hydrogel lenses were invented in 1998 he added those too.
notes: Very private, with no website, social media or family office found. Not to be confused with racing driver or other Alan Wells. The web-search budget ran out mid-lane, so his post-2014 activities and alive status were not verified. Low podcast fit.

name: Christopher Lee-Smith
current_role: Co-Founder, Global Head of Distribution and Director, Accelerant Holdings (NYSE: ARX)
profile: Christopher Lee-Smith (57 at the 2025 IPO) co-founded Accelerant, a 'Risk Exchange' that connects specialty-insurance MGAs with risk capital using a data and technology platform. Before Accelerant he was Global Head of Alternative Distribution at Argo Group (2017–2018). Accelerant listed on the NYSE in July 2025 at $21 a share, and he has worked on assignment in Malta for the company.
interesting_fact: Accelerant, a 'Risk Exchange' for specialty insurance, grew from a startup to a NYSE listing within about seven years (founded 2018, IPO July 2025). It earns fees for services to MGAs and to the risk capital behind them rather than acting as a traditional insurer.
deep_cut_fact: Per the IPO founders' letter, Accelerant began in Stockholm in 2018. The founders watched a talented underwriter at an MGA struggle to price a risk because of slow transactions, short-term contracts and poor data, and decided 'Something had to change.'
notes: Insurtech operator rather than energy/data-centre. CEO Jeff Radke is the public face. No published press email found (the website didn't render without JavaScript); check accelerant.ai or the investor site for an IR/press contact. LinkedIn is the likely best route.

name: Thomas D Logan
current_role: Founder, Chief Executive Officer (since 2005) and Chairman (since Feb 2025), Mirion Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: MIR)
profile: Tom Logan founded Mirion Technologies in 2005 and has run it ever since. Mirion makes radiation detection, measurement and dosimetry technology for nuclear power, defence and cancer care, and it went public in October 2021 by merging with Goldman Sachs' SPAC GS Acquisition Holdings II. He has been steering it toward nuclear power, which made up about 47% of revenue after the 2025 Certrec and Paragon Energy Solutions deals.
interesting_fact: Mirion's 2026 proxy ties its growth directly to AI. It says power availability for data centres and AI infrastructure is driving momentum in nuclear, and Mirion is positioning for advanced and small modular reactors.
deep_cut_fact: Before Mirion he started out in finance roles at Chevron. He was then CFO of E-M Solutions and BVP, President of BAF Energy, and CEO of radiation-dosimetry firm Global Dosimetry Solutions (2004–05). He holds both his B.S. and MBA from Cornell.
notes: Excellent podcast fit, sitting at the intersection of nuclear power, SMRs and AI data-centre power demand. Reach him through Mirion IR/communications (ir@mirion.com).

name: Ravi P Agrawal
current_role: Member of the Agrawal promoter family of Ajanta Pharma Ltd (NSE: AJANTPHARM); no board or executive role listed on the company website
profile: Ravi P. Agrawal appears on Hurun India (2018–2019) through the Agrawal family's stake in Mumbai-based Ajanta Pharma. Ajanta is a specialty pharma company selling branded generics in India, Asia, the Middle East and Africa, plus US generics, from seven Indian plants. He is not on the current board, and he is presumably part of the promoter group (the 'P' likely refers to Purushottam Agrawal).
interesting_fact: Ajanta sells in 34+ countries, has 850+ R&D scientists and focuses on being '1st to market' with niche molecules in Indian branded generics.
notes: Identity only partly confirmed. He is not among Ajanta's directors, so his exact relationship (promoter-group shareholder) needs checking in the shareholding pattern. The public faces are chairman Purushottam Agrawal and MD Yogesh Agrawal, and an approach should go via company channels. Not an energy/data-centre fit.

name: Kamalkumar Shivkishan Agrawal
current_role: Director in the Nagpur arm of the Haldiram's group (Haldiram Foods International / Haldiram's India Pvt Ltd), part of the Shiv Kishan Agrawal family
profile: Kamal Kumar Agrawal is a son of Shiv Kishan Agrawal, who leads the Nagpur branch of Haldiram's. The snack and sweets business was founded in Bikaner in 1937 by his great-grandfather Ganga Bhishen 'Haldiram' Agarwal. In the 2022–25 restructuring, the Nagpur family took a 44% stake in the merged packaged-snacks company Haldiram Snacks Food, which Temasek invested in in 2025 at about a US$10bn valuation.
interesting_fact: Haldiram's began in 1937 as a single sweets-and-namkeen shop in Bikaner. In 2017 it overtook PepsiCo to become India's largest snack company, and in 2025 Temasek bought a 9%+ stake at about a US$10bn valuation.
notes: Very low media profile; the family speaks through patriarch Shiv Kishan Agrawal. His exact current title was not verified in filings. Not an energy fit, though the Temasek deal and the family-business transition could make a story. Avoid older family legal matters.
